lines.text: I came down out of the White onto the north field at noon. The Skeld were waiting, as if they had known. Yrsa stood in the snow facing me, with her blind white eyes.
Warm One. Your people are bleeding. Breathe the way I taught you. And this time, open every door you have.
I knelt in the snow on my own land, and pressed my bare black hands flat against the earth.
I could feel all of them. Every thread in Greyhollow. Bram, bleeding in the gate. Tobin. Kell. Agna. Three half-grown pups. And Ash.
At Kesting, I had opened every door at once. This time, I took the doors off their hinges.
It went out of me like the sea.
The snow went first. Across the whole valley, in one breath, like a sheet pulled off a bed. Underneath, the fields were green.
Then the light reached the gate. Every one of my people lit up like a lamp. Threes and fours stood up as fives. For one night, Greyhollow was a village of lords.
And Bram went through the ceiling.
Six rings. There were three men alive in Aldmere who could say that. For one night, a one-armed steward from Greyhollow made four.
No. That's not possible. Rings don't...
Rings don't grow. I know, my lord. I've heard.
Bram swung once. Penhallow's borrowed fire went out like a candle dropped in a bucket, and he went down on his back in the slush.
Then, from the west, a horn. Then a hundred horns.
Kesting! Kesting and the boy! Forward, you lazy bears!
Halvard's column came down the west road into the back of Penhallow's army, with the Old Bear roaring at the front like the beast on his banner. The army broke like ice in spring.
Penhallow got up. He didn't run. I'll give him that much. There was nowhere left for him to run to.
The Grand Measurer will burn this valley, steward. Every field. Every child.
Not while I'm in it.
His ring flickered, the way it had in my bathhouse. For a heartbeat, he looked like a very tired man. Then Bram's sword came down, and Lord Penhallow was finished.
I didn't see any of it. By then I was lying face down in the green grass of the north field, with Yrsa holding my head in her lap, and my hands black to the knuckles.
I slept for three weeks.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and twenty, coming soon.
